questions.stem: At night you see an all-round white light forward and a second, lower all-round white light near the stern of a large ship. No sidelights are visible. What is she doing?
options: Aground
At anchor
Underway and making way
Towing
questions.explanation: Rule 30(a): a forward all-round white light and a lower all-round white light at or near the stern is the anchor signal. Aground adds two all-round reds, an underway vessel shows sidelights, and a towing vessel shows masthead lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: What lights and day shapes does a 60 m vessel aground show?
options: Two all-round red lights only; by day two balls
Anchor lights plus two reds; three balls by day
Anchor lights only; by day one ball
Three all-round red lights; by day a cylinder
questions.explanation: Rule 30(d): a vessel aground shows the anchor lights and two all-round reds in a vertical line, and by day three balls. Two reds or two balls alone is not under command, three reds or a cylinder is constrained by draught, and anchor lights or one ball alone is simply at anchor.

questions.stem: A 35 m vessel is at anchor overnight. Which is a legal way for her to show she is at anchor?
options: Two all-round red lights in a line
One all-round white where best seen
Sidelights and a sternlight
A masthead light only, switched on
questions.explanation: Rule 30(b) lets a vessel under 50 m show one all-round white light where it can best be seen instead of the two anchor lights. Sidelights and sternlight would mean she is underway, two reds mean NUC, and a masthead light is not an anchor light.

questions.stem: Which vessel at anchor is required to illuminate her decks with her working or equivalent lights?
options: Only a vessel carrying dangerous goods
Every vessel at anchor
A vessel of 100 m or more in length
A vessel of 50 m or more in length
questions.explanation: Rule 30(c): any vessel at anchor may illuminate her decks, and a vessel of 100 m or more shall. 50 m is the threshold for the single anchor light option, not deck lights.

questions.stem: Which small-vessel exemptions does Rule 30 give?
options: Under 7 m anchored clear of traffic: none; under 12 m aground: none
A vessel under 12 m never needs anchor lights; a vessel under 20 m aground needs no signals
A vessel under 7 m aground need not show anchor lights; a vessel under 12 m at anchor needs only a ball
There are no small-vessel exemptions in Rule 30
questions.explanation: Rule 30(e) exempts a vessel under 7 m at anchor only when she is not in or near a narrow channel, fairway or anchorage or where other vessels normally navigate. Rule 30(f) exempts a vessel under 12 m aground from the two reds and three balls, but not from her anchor signals.

questions.stem: Under Annex I, when a vessel carries two anchor lights, how are they placed relative to each other?
options: The forward light at least 4.5 m above the after light
The forward light at least 1 m above the after light
Both at the same height
The after light at least 4.5 m above the forward light
questions.explanation: Annex I section 2(k): the forward anchor light is not less than 4.5 m above the after one, and on a vessel of 50 m or more it is at least 6 m above the hull. Rule 30(a) also says the stern light is at a lower level. The after light is never the higher one.

questions.stem: A string of log booms is anchored in a recognized booming area within a BC harbour, away from the fairway and from where vessels normally navigate. Under the Canadian modification, which statement is correct?
options: The booms must show the normal anchor lights of Rule 30(a)
The booms must show an all-round white light at each corner
No light is required in that area
The booms must show two all-round red lights
questions.explanation: Rule 30(h), a Canadian modification for Canadian inland waters, says a barge or inconspicuous, partly submerged object at anchor need not show any light while inside a recognized mooring, storage or booming area that is not in or near a narrow channel or fairway or where other vessels normally navigate. The other options would apply only outside that exemption, if at all. Expect unlit obstructions near booming grounds.
